content.text: This is a purely presentational client component. Let me verify by checking the DetailItem type and any callers to understand data provenance.

Analysis complete. **Phase 1 — Entry points/sinks:** This is a purely presentational Next.js client component. It renders props (item/stats/goesWith), wires two navigation buttons, and renders images and links. No exec/SQL/eval/fs/HTTP sinks, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, no deserialization, no template engines, no logging. **Phase 2 — Data flow:** All rendered values come from typed `DetailItem`/`GoesWithCard` props sourced by the shell from the app's own database. React text interpolation escapes automatically. `` does not execute `javascript:` URLs. `` uses a DB-generated id; even if it contained slashes/`..`, Next.js `` treats it as a client-side URL — worst case is a broken navigation, not a security boundary crossing (no callbacks receive it). **Phase 2b/c — patterns:** - No parser/validator changes. - Callbacks (`onEdit`, `onArchive`) are just fired on click — the parent supplies the action; this component doesn't authorize anything. - `router.push("/closet")` is a static path, not user data. - No new registries, gates, allowlists, or teardown of identity primitives. - Tests are pure render assertions with mocked `next/navigation`. No security-relevant sinks are introduced by this change.
